items.q: CRAB features defining active myeloma stand for which four damages?
o: Hypercalcaemia, renal failure, anaemia and bone lesions
items.exp: CRAB is hyperCalcaemia, Renal impairment, Anaemia and Bone lesions attributable to the plasma clone, separating treatable myeloma from MGUS observation. Modern biomarkers (marrow burden, light chain ratio, MRI lesions) can also define activity.
r: Incorrect. Those are non specific symptom lists.
Correct. Calcium, renal, anaemia, bone equals CRAB.
Incorrect. That mixes neurology and allergy features.
Incorrect. That describes lymphoma staging features.
items.kp: CRAB decides treat versus watch in plasma clones.

items.q: Punched out lytic bone lesions without sclerotic rim, rouleaux and IgG spike in an older adult indicate what?
items.exp: Myeloma osteoclast activation dissolves bone purely lytically (prostate metastases are sclerotic instead), with monoclonal IgG, rouleaux from paraprotein coating and marrow plasmacytosis.
r: Incorrect. Prostate metastases are osteoblastic sclerotic.
Correct. Pure lytic punches mean myeloma.
Incorrect. Waldenstrom spares bone with IgM viscosity.
Incorrect. Paget remodels thickened sclerotic bone with high ALP.
items.kp: Lytic holes plus spike equals myeloma; sclerotic equals prostate.

items.q: Monoclonal IgM with hyperviscosity visual changes, bleeding and lymphadenopathy but no bone lesions indicate what?
items.exp: Waldenstrom secretes pentameric IgM raising viscosity (blurred vision, epistaxis, neuropathy) infiltrating marrow and nodes without osteolysis, MYD88 mutated in most, plasmapheresis for symptomatic viscosity.
r: Incorrect. True IgM myeloma is vanishingly rare and lytic.
Correct. IgM viscosity without bone disease is Waldenstrom.
Incorrect. MGUS by definition lacks symptoms needing therapy.
Incorrect. CLL is lymphocytic without IgM viscosity definition.
items.kp: IgM plus sludge minus bone holes equals Waldenstrom.

items.q: Myeloma kidney failure is driven mainly by which tubular injury?
o: Free light chain casts obstructing tubules with Tamm Horfall protein (cast nephropathy)
items.exp: Filtered free light chains precipitate with Tamm Horsfall protein in distal tubules forming obstructing fractured casts with giant cell reaction, worsened by dehydration, hypercalcaemia and nephrotoxins needing rapid clone reduction.
r: Incorrect. Amyloid is glomerular in a minority complication.
Correct. Light chain cast nephropathy blocks tubules.
Incorrect. Calcium contributes but casts dominate pathology.
Incorrect. Interstitial tumour invasion is uncommon cause.
items.kp: Light chains cast tubules shut: hydrate and kill the clone fast.

items.q: MGUS progresses to myeloma at approximately what average yearly rate, guiding observation not treatment?
items.exp: MGUS (small clone, no damage) transforms at roughly one percent yearly (higher with large IgA or abnormal light chain ratio), so surveillance without chemotherapy balances benefit and harm.
r: Incorrect. That rate fits high risk smouldering disease more.
Correct. About one percent yearly for MGUS.
Incorrect. Risk persists lifelong, never zero.
Incorrect. That urgency would mandate immediate therapy.
items.kp: MGUS creeps at one percent a year: watch, do not blast.

items.q: Overwhelming post splenectomy infection is feared from which organism group needing vaccination?
o: Encapsulated bacteria: pneumococcus, meningococcus, Haemophilus influenzae b
items.exp: Splenic marginal zone clears encapsulated bacteria opsonised poorly without it, causing fulminant OPSI sepsis, so vaccination (pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib) plus education and standby antibiotics are lifelong.
r: Incorrect. Gut anaerobes cause abdominal sepsis differently.
Correct. Encapsulated organisms kill asplenic patients.
Incorrect. Fungi threaten neutropenia more than asplenia.
Incorrect. Viruses are controlled by cellular immunity intact here.
items.kp: No spleen means vaccinate against capsules for life.

items.q: Ferritin extremely high with cytopenias, fever, splenomegaly and macrophages eating blood cells in marrow indicate which emergency?
items.exp: HLH is hyperinflammatory macrophage activation (primary genetic or secondary to EBV, lymphoma, autoimmunity) with ferritin storms, cytopenias and haemophagocytosis needing immunosuppression and trigger treatment urgently.
r: Incorrect. Haemochromatosis loads iron without this cytokine storm.
Correct. Ferritin storm plus eating macrophages means HLH.
Incorrect. Gaucher is chronic storage without acute storm.
Incorrect. Aplasia lacks activated haemophagocytosis and fever storm.
items.kp: Ferritin through the roof plus eaten cells equals HLH. Move fast.

items.q: Lytic skull lesions, diabetes insipidus and eczema like rash in a child with Birbeck granules indicate what?
items.exp: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (CD1a, langerin, tennis racket Birbeck granules, often BRAF mutated) causes punched skull lesions, pituitary stalk diabetes insipidus and seborrhoeic rash in children, staged single versus multisystem.
r: Incorrect. Ewing is a bone sarcoma without granule histiocytes.
Correct. Birbeck granules mean Langerhans histiocytosis.
Incorrect. Neuroblastoma metastases lack this rash pituitary pattern.
Incorrect. Infection lacks clonal Birbeck cells.
items.kp: Tennis racket granules in a child equal Langerhans disease.

items.q: Smouldering myeloma differs from MGUS and active myeloma how?
o: It has CRAB damage needing therapy
Higher clone burden (10 to 60 percent or large M protein) without end organ damage, observed with early intervention trials
It is a benign reactive plasmacytosis
items.exp: Smouldering disease carries myeloma defining clone burden without CRAB or biomarkers, progressing about ten percent yearly early, managed by observation or trial early therapy rather than standard treatment.
r: Incorrect. CRAB would make it active myeloma.
Correct. Big clone, no damage: smouldering observation.
Incorrect. Monoclonal protein is present and larger.
Incorrect. It is clonal, not reactive.
items.kp: Smouldering means loaded but not yet damaging. Watch closely.

items.q: Bone pain with hypercalcaemia in myeloma results from osteoclast activation driven notably by which marrow signal?
o: RANKL excess with osteoblast suppression (DKK1), causing pure lysis without healing sclerosis
Parathyroid hormone secretion by myeloma cells
items.exp: Myeloma niche raises RANKL and suppresses osteoblasts via DKK1, so bone dissolves without reactive formation (cold on bone scans, punched radiographs) releasing calcium. Bisphosphonates or denosumab protect skeleton.
r: Incorrect. Osteoprotegerin blocks RANKL protectively, and it is reduced relatively.
Correct. RANKL up, osteoblasts down: pure lysis.
Incorrect. Myeloma does not secrete PTH; calcium is skeletal.
Incorrect. Vitamin D is not marrow produced here.
items.kp: Myeloma melts bone silently: lytic, cold scans, high calcium.
